name: Bluesky
description: Bluesky is a decentralized social network built on the open AT Protocol. People and organizations use it to publish posts, follow accounts, and participate in portable public conversations.
agentUseSummary: Connect one account through AT Protocol OAuth, then let agents read the exact bound profile, list up to ten original posts, draft locally, and publish one approval-controlled text post without exposing tokens, DPoP keys, or raw XRPC access.

capabilities.label: Read profile
capabilities.description: Read the public profile for the exact OAuth-bound DID.

capabilities.label: Read own posts
capabilities.description: List at most ten original no-embed posts authored by the bound DID.

capabilities.label: Draft text post
capabilities.description: Draft one 1–300-grapheme text post locally with no provider side effect.

capabilities.label: Publish text post
capabilities.description: Publish one exact text-only app.bsky.feed.post record.

allowed.label: Read bound profile
allowed.description: Read provider-correct public fields for the exact OAuth-bound DID.

allowed.label: List own original posts
allowed.description: List at most ten original no-embed posts authored by the bound DID without pagination.

allowed.label: Draft text post
allowed.description: Prepare one normalized 1–300-grapheme text post locally.

approvalRequired.label: Publish text post
approvalRequired.description: Create one exact approval-controlled text-only record on the bound PDS.

blocked.label: Block broader social actions
blocked.description: Replies, quotes, reposts, likes, follows, deletes, media, embeds, facets, links, private data, discovery, chat, moderation, firehose, pagination, and bulk actions are not registered.

blocked.label: Block raw and unbound access
blocked.description: Transition scopes, arbitrary XRPC, alternate identities, unverified PDS or issuer endpoints, private-network answers, redirects, token exposure, and automatic write retry are unavailable.

approvalProfiles.label: Safe
approvalProfiles.description: Bound-profile reads, bounded own-post reads, and local drafts run automatically; exact text publishing requires approval.

approvalProfiles.label: Dangerously skip permissions
approvalProfiles.description: All four selected Bluesky actions run without Relay per-action approval; exact identity binding, bounds, DPoP, audits, secret isolation, and no-retry behavior still apply.

runtimeSupport.description: Relay mounts four typed Bluesky wrappers and attaches the encrypted DPoP-bound token only inside Railway's exact DID, PDS, and issuer adapter.
Relay mounts four typed Bluesky wrappers and attaches the encrypted DPoP-bound token only inside Railway's exact DID, PDS, and issuer adapter.

providerSetup.blocker: The sharded worker may not deploy Railway or run live AT Protocol consent; staging deployment and representative-account OAuth acceptance remain for the integration and provider-console tasks.
providerSetup.nextAction: After batch integration, deploy only Railway staging, then use the separate provider-console task to validate public client metadata, dynamic discovery, PAR, PKCE, DPoP nonce handling, issuer and exact DID/PDS binding, bounded reads, approved and dangerous-mode publishing, revocation, SSRF and redirect denial, and post-disconnect denial.

evidence.supports: Bluesky documents public OAuth client metadata, authorization-code flow, PKCE, PAR, DPoP, callbacks, token refresh, and revocation.
The AT Protocol OAuth profile defines protected-resource and authorization-server discovery, issuer binding, public clients, PKCE, PAR, DPoP, token subject binding, and callback issuer handling.
AT Protocol permission-set guidance documents granular repository scopes and warns that transition:generic grants broad account access.
The granular permission syntax supports create-only access for the app.bsky.feed.post collection.
The Bluesky API documents bounded author-feed reads used for the exact-own-post wrapper.
AT Protocol documents creation of app.bsky.feed.post records and the 300-grapheme text limit.
